title: embeddings-rerank-incident-scratch-oliver-gomez-2026-03-20
content:
Purpose:
Quick scratchpad for the embeddings->rerank pipeline anomalies observed 2026-03-19 -> 2026-03-20. Notes compiled while debugging. Not a postmortem yet - saving breadcrumbs for follow-up and handoff.

Summary of symptoms:
- Intermittent 400 errors from rerank endpoint that complain about embedding dimension mismatch.
  - Error example: 'ValueError: embedding vector length 1536 does not match model expected 1024' (see logs below).
- Concurrent with dimension errors we saw occasional p95 latency spikes for the rerank endpoint (normal p95 ~ 120ms, spikes up to 900ms).
- Approx timeline: first alerts 2026-03-19 22:40 UTC; spike cluster 22:40-23:10; continued low rate errors through 03-20.

Live-checks run (commands tried):
1) Quick curl against embeddings service (to validate returned dim):
   curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.internal/v1/embeddings -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACT' -d '{"model":"embed-alpha-2","input":"test string"}' | jq '.data[0].embedding | length'
   -> returned 1536 during suspicious window (expected 1024 for embed-alpha-1 family).

2) Python/SDK call to reranker (local repro):
   from redwood import RedwoodClient
   c = RedwoodClient(token='REDACT')
   q_emb = c.embeddings.create(model='embed-alpha-2', input='query')
   docs_emb = [c.embeddings.create(model='embed-alpha-2', input=d) for d in docs]
   r = c.rerank.create(model='rerank-v1', query_embedding=q_emb, document_embeddings=docs_emb)
   -> raised ValueError: 'embedding vector length 1536 does not match model expected 1024'

3) Direct hits to model metadata endpoint to see expected dims:
   curl -s https://model-catalog.internal/v1/models/embed-alpha-2 | jq '.output_dimensions'
   -> returns 1536 (consistent).
   curl -s https://model-catalog.internal/v1/models/rerank-v1 | jq '.expected_input_dim'
   -> returns 1024

4) Check rollout history for embed models (k8s annotations + release engineer notes):
   kubectl -n models get deploy embed-alpha-2 -o yaml | grep image
   -> image tag shows 'embed-alpha-2:2026-03-18-rc3' (recent).

Relevant logs / error snippets (redacted):
- 2026-03-19T22:45:12Z [rerank-worker-12] ERROR ValueError: embedding vector length 1536 does not match model expected 1024 (trace id: xxxxx)
- 2026-03-19T22:46:03Z [emb-service-03] INFO returned embedding len=1536 model=embed-alpha-2 req_id=yyyyy
- 2026-03-19T22:47:55Z [router] WARN route mismatch: request for rerank-v1 routed to rerank-v1-variant-b (expected variant-a)
- 2026-03-19T22:48:10Z [metrics] p95_rerank_ms=920 host=rerank-node-07

Initial hypotheses (ranked):
1) Model mismatch between embedding generator and reranker expected dims: someone switched the default embed model used by the client or platform from embed-alpha-1 (1024) to embed-alpha-2 (1536) without upgrading rerank model or adapter.
   - Evidence: embeddings service returning 1536, model catalog shows new embed model default, rerank-v1 expects 1024.

2) Partial rollout / routing inconsistency: router occasionally routes requests to an older rerank variant that expects different input shape or to a rerank that was compiled against a different embedding dim. This could create both mismatch errors and latency when runtime attempts shape conversions/fails over.
   - Evidence: router logs show 'route mismatch' warning around same time.

3) Backwards-incompatible embed model release (embed-alpha-2) was pushed without updating the integration test matrix; client libraries might still default to older names leading to on-the-wire mixing of embedding dims across services.

4) Batching behavior + lazy upcasting: if embeddings are batched differently (some 1024, some 1536) the reranker may attempt to pad/convert which increases CPU and causes p95 spikes. (Less likely given explicit dimension error, but worth checking batcher code paths.)

Immediate checks / actions taken: 
- Reproduced locally using exact SDK calls -> consistent dimension error.
- Validated model catalog expected dims for both models (embed_alpha_2 =1536, rerank_v1 =1024).
- Queried feature flags and client config service to confirm whether default embed model changed: feature-flags shows 'default.embed_model=embed-alpha-2' since 2026-03-18 18:12 UTC.
- Pulled recent deploy PRs: PR 456 for embed-alpha-2 rollouts merged 2026-03-18 (link in linked_artifacts).

Mitigations applied / considered: 
- Hot fix option A (short-term): revert default.embed_model to embed-alpha-1 via config service to stop new requests using 1536-dim embeddings. Pros: quick rollback, reduces new errors. Cons: does not fix existing cached/doc embeddings already 1536-length.
- Hot fix option B: Push compatibility adapter on rerank layer that accepts 1536 and reduces/pools to 1024 (unsafe, lossy). Risky for accuracy.
- Hot fix option C: Deploy updated rerank variant compiled for 1536 and route embed-alpha-2 -> rerank-v1-1536. Safer but requires deploy cadence and QA.
- Immediate applied: toggled default.embed_model back to embed-alpha-1 to stop new traffic (2026-03-20 00:05 UTC). Monitoring alert: new error rate fell ~90% within 15 mins.

Outstanding anomalies to investigate (notes for SRE / eng):
- Why did client config/feature flag change default without a coordinated multi-team rollout? Check the change author and associated checklist. (JIRA-IR-7890 created).
- Why did router route to rerank variant-b? Is there a routing table drift or stale config cached on some nodes? Check router caches and config sync (see router logs at router-logs-2026-03-19.gz).
- Latency spikes: correlate with nodes that attempted conversions or had high CPU while dealing with unexpected embedding shapes. Grab flamegraphs for rerank-node-07 for the spike window.
- Existing embeddings in DB/index: some previously indexed document embeddings might now be 1536 (if batch reindexing or one-off jobs ran). Need to audit stored embedding dims in vector DB (call: SELECT count(*) FROM embeddings WHERE dim != 1024).

Debugging checklist / commands for follow-up:
- Re-run spot checks across multiple regions:
  - curl to embeddings endpoint and count dims for a sample of requests over 1h window.
  - query model-catalog for expected dims for all active embed models.
- On rerank nodes (prod):
  - sudo journalctl -u rerank.service --since '2026-03-19 22:30' --until '2026-03-19 23:30' > /tmp/rerank-22-30.log
  - run pprof/async-profiler for pid at 22:48:10 to capture spike
- Vector DB audit (approx SQL commands):
  - SELECT model_name, COUNT(*) FROM embeddings GROUP BY model_name ORDER BY COUNT DESC;
  - SELECT COUNT(*) FROM embeddings WHERE dim NOT IN (1024,1536);
- Confirm which clients/services pulled the new default: search for 'default.embed_model' change in audits and deploy logs.

Notes for postmortem skeleton (what to include):
- Timeline with detection/mitigation timestamps
- Impact: number of failed requests, affected customers (if any), latency SLO breaches
- Root cause analysis: pinpoint whether root cause is config change, model rollout, router drift, or a combination
- Corrective actions: config/feature flag gating, automated compatibility tests in CI, integration tests between embed and rerank models, routing consistency checks, alerting improvements (detect dim mismatch earlier)
- Owners and follow-ups: Eng-applied-ml to own model compatibility tests, Platform/Infra to own router cache invalidation fix, SRE to own latency instrumentation follow-ups.

Random notes / hypotheses to verify later:
- Could quantization/packing reduce dim requirement? Probably not - dim is structural.
- Did a previous A/B test leave a variant active in some regions? Check regional rollout logs.
- Re-ranker may have older compiled kernels that assume 1024; deploying a 1536-optimized rerank build should reduce CPU conversion attempts and likely reduce p95.

Next steps (immediate owners):
- Oliver: finish audit of stored embeddings and share counts with team by EOD.
- Maya: check feature-flag change author and roll history; block further changes until gating in place.
- Ryan: capture pprof from rerank-node-07 and upload to /tmp/incident-analysis/.
- Samira: work with infra to verify router caches and force a config refresh if needed.

If anything useful pops up while I'm AFK, leave notes here. Will convert to a formal incident report once we confirm root cause.

End of scratchpad.
